title: Scalable Differentiable Causal Discovery in the Presence of Latent Confounders with Skeleton Posterior

problem.claim: Real-world causal discovery must address ubiquitous latent confounders and the need to learn maximal ancestral graphs.

gap.claim: Existing differentiable maximal ancestral graph learning algorithms have been limited to small datasets and have not scaled to datasets with more than 50 variables.

narrative_sequence.summary: Differentiable causal discovery has advanced the learning of directed acyclic graphs.
Latent confounders and scalability limitations restrict the application of differentiable causal discovery to real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract units do not state the proposed method or explain the role of the skeleton posterior.
No theoretical results, experiments, datasets, baselines, quantitative findings, or limitations are supplied.
The abstract units do not establish any contribution beyond the problem and scalability gap.
